message.content:
In French, “hello” is most commonly translated as **“bonjour.”**  
It’s a polite greeting you use during daylight hours (morning through late afternoon).  

If it’s after sunset, people usually say **“bonsoir,”** which literally means “good evening.”  

For informal situations among friends or peers, especially at night, many simply say **“salut,”** similar to English “hi.”

So:

| Context | Common Greeting |
|---------|----------------|
| Daytime (any time before dusk) | *Bonjour* |
| Evening/night | *Bonsoir* |
| Informal/friendly anytime | *Salut* |

These words carry the same friendly intent as saying “hello” in English.
